intro: Excerpts copied from the live QI Brain source (C:\QIH\engine\brain). Each shows the real code behind a capability and explains how it works. The Brain follows two rules visible throughout: all logic lives in api.py (the MCP server is a thin client), and nothing about the LLMs is hardcoded — providers live in the llm_providers table.

snippets.title: The single WAL-mode connection factory
snippets.feature: open_brain_db — every module's one way into qi_brain.db
snippets.code:
_THIS_DIR    = Path(__file__).parent                  # engine/brain/core/
_PROJECT_DIR = _THIS_DIR.parent.parent.parent         # C:\QIH
_DATA_DIR    = _PROJECT_DIR / "data"
DB_PATH      = Path(os.environ.get("QI_BRAIN_DB", str(_DATA_DIR / "qi_brain.db")))

def open_brain_db(path: Path = DB_PATH) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    conn = sqlite3.connect(str(path), check_same_thread=False)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
    return conn
snippets.explanation: Every module that touches the database goes through this one helper, so the critical PRAGMAs are applied on every connection: WAL journal mode (concurrent writers don't block readers), a 5-second busy timeout (so a brief lock retries instead of erroring), and foreign_keys ON (referential integrity is enforced, not advisory). The DB lives at C:\QIH\data\qi_brain.db and can be redirected with the QI_BRAIN_DB env var for tests.

snippets.title: Schema DDL — the decisions ledger with supersede
snippets.feature: Decision ledger that records why, by whom, and what replaced it
snippets.code:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS decisions (
    decision_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    project_id       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(project_id),
    agent_id         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'claude' REFERENCES agents(agent_id),
    decision_code    TEXT UNIQUE,   -- e.g. 'AD-001'
    title            TEXT NOT NULL,
    rationale        TEXT NOT NULL,
    impact_scope     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'project',  -- project|ecosystem|global
    tags             TEXT,          -- JSON array of strings
    superseded_by    INTEGER REFERENCES decisions(decision_id),
    superseded_at    TEXT,
    superseded_reason TEXT,
    recorded_at      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_decisions_active
    ON decisions(superseded_by) WHERE superseded_by IS NULL;
snippets.explanation: Decisions are append-only and self-referential: a reversed decision is never deleted — it gets a superseded_by pointer to the decision that replaced it, plus a reason. The partial index on superseded_by IS NULL makes 'give me the still-active decisions' fast, which is exactly what qi_get_context asks for. Every row records the agent_id that logged it and the impact_scope that controls how far the decision reaches.

snippets.title: ChromaDB collections with cosine similarity
snippets.feature: Semantic memory store — 4 collections, local embeddings
snippets.explanation: The vector half of the dual store. A persistent ChromaDB client at qi_memory/ holds four collections — one each for decisions, features, sessions and ecosystem docs — every one configured for cosine similarity (the right metric for normalized text embeddings). get_or_create_collection makes initialization idempotent, so the store self-heals if a collection is missing on boot.

snippets.title: Embed + upsert a decision
snippets.feature: Vectorize text so it can be recalled by meaning
snippets.code:
async def add_decision(self, decision_id, text, metadata=None):
    vec = await self._embed(text)
    col = self._get_col(COL_DECISIONS)
    col.upsert(
        ids=[f"decision_{decision_id}"],
        embeddings=[vec],
        documents=[text],
        metadatas=[metadata or {}],
    )

async def _embed(self, text: str) -> list[float]:
    embedder = self._get_embedder()   # lazy: ProviderFactory.get_by_role('embed')
    return await embedder.embed(text)
snippets.explanation: Each decision is upserted under a stable id (decision_{id}) so re-logging overwrites rather than duplicating. The embedding vector comes from whatever provider holds the 'embed' role in the DB — currently local nomic-embed-text — resolved lazily on first use. Metadata (project_id, scope) rides along so searches can be filtered by project.

snippets.title: Semantic search across a collection
snippets.feature: qi_search_memory — find anything by meaning, not keywords
snippets.code:
async def search(self, query, collection=COL_DECISIONS, n=5, where=None):
    vec = await self._embed(query)
    col = self._get_col(collection)
    kwargs = {"query_embeddings": [vec], "n_results": n,
              "include": ["documents", "metadatas", "distances"]}
    if where:
        kwargs["where"] = where
    results = col.query(**kwargs)
    output = []
    for i, doc_id in enumerate(results["ids"][0]):
        output.append({
            "id":       doc_id,
            "document": results["documents"][0][i],
            "metadata": results["metadatas"][0][i],
            "distance": results["distances"][0][i],
        })
    return output
snippets.explanation: The query string is embedded with the same model used for the stored documents, then ChromaDB returns the n closest by cosine distance. An optional where filter (e.g. {project_id: 'maia'}) scopes the search. The flat list of {id, document, metadata, distance} is what the qi_search_memory MCP tool hands back to a Claude session.

snippets.title: The app + open CORS for QI services
snippets.feature: Single FastAPI app any QI project can call
snippets.code:
app = FastAPI(
    title="QI Brain API",
    version="002",
    description="Shared knowledge substrate for the QI ecosystem",
)

# CORS — allow all QI services
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["*"],
    allow_credentials=False,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)
snippets.explanation: One app exposes the whole Brain on port 9011. CORS is wide-open because the Brain is deployed local-only behind the QI service boundary — any QI project (current or future) can call it from a browser with no per-project allow-listing. (Locking this down with auth is the headline release-hardening item before any remote exposure.)

snippets.title: Health / version / info probes
snippets.feature: Monitorable service — validator + uptime checks
snippets.explanation: Standard QI service probes. /health is the cheap liveness check the QI_BrainAPI service monitor and qi_validator hit; /info advertises the Brain's capabilities and counts its own routes. These are why 'Brain API (:9011) down' has a one-line diagnosis in QI_Service_Registry.md.

snippets.title: Project-id resolution — typos never become 500s
snippets.feature: Robust input handling for cross-project callers
snippets.explanation: Because many different agents and services call the Brain, a mistyped project_id is inevitable. Rather than letting a bad id reach the DB and blow up as an opaque FOREIGN KEY 500, this resolver normalizes case/whitespace/hyphens, tries a separator-insensitive match, and as a last resort returns a clean HTTP 400 with did-you-mean suggestions and the full valid list. Every write endpoint runs through it.

snippets.title: log_decision — write-through to both stores
snippets.feature: qi_log_decision MCP tool
snippets.code:
@app.post("/api/log_decision")
async def log_decision(req: LogDecisionRequest):
    tags_json = json.dumps(req.tags or [])
    with open_brain_db() as conn:
        req.project_id = _resolve_pid(conn, req.project_id)
        cur = conn.execute(
            """INSERT INTO decisions
                 (project_id, agent_id, decision_code, title, rationale, impact_scope, tags)
               VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
            (req.project_id, req.agent_id, req.decision_code,
             req.title, req.rationale, req.impact_scope, tags_json))
        decision_id = cur.lastrowid
        conn.commit()
    try:
        await _memory().add_decision(decision_id, f"{req.title}\n{req.rationale}",
            metadata={"project_id": req.project_id, "scope": req.impact_scope})
    except Exception:
        pass  # DB write succeeded; Chroma failure is non-fatal
    return {"ok": True, "decision_id": decision_id}
snippets.explanation: The canonical write pattern. The SQL INSERT is authoritative and committed first; only then is the title+rationale embedded into ChromaDB. The embed is wrapped in a bare except so that if the vector store is unavailable the structured record still lands — the Brain treats SQL as truth and Chroma as a rebuildable index. tags are stored as a JSON string in a single column.

snippets.title: get_context — ranked, token-budgeted briefing
snippets.feature: qi_get_context — orient a fresh session in one call
snippets.code:
days = int(_cfg("context_days", "14"))
cutoff = (datetime.now() - timedelta(days=days)).isoformat()

decisions = conn.execute("""
    SELECT d.decision_id, d.decision_code, d.title, d.rationale,
           d.impact_scope, d.tags, d.project_id, d.recorded_at
    FROM decisions d
    WHERE d.superseded_by IS NULL
      AND (d.project_id = ? OR d.impact_scope IN ('ecosystem','global'))
      AND d.recorded_at >= ?
    ORDER BY
        CASE WHEN d.project_id = ? THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
        d.recorded_at DESC
    LIMIT 50
""", (req.project_id, cutoff, req.project_id)).fetchall()
snippets.explanation: The most-called tool. It selects only still-active decisions (superseded_by IS NULL) that either belong to the asking project OR carry ecosystem/global scope (rulings that bind everyone), inside a 14-day window. The ORDER BY puts the project's own decisions first, then newest-first. The caller then walks this list accumulating estimated tokens and stops at token_budget — so the briefing is relevant AND fits the context window.

snippets.title: supersede_decision — reverse without forgetting
snippets.feature: qi_supersede_decision (Supplement A I-08)
snippets.code:
@app.post("/api/supersede_decision")
async def supersede_decision(req: SupersedeDecisionRequest):
    with open_brain_db() as conn:
        old = conn.execute("SELECT decision_id FROM decisions WHERE decision_id=?",
                           (req.old_decision_id,)).fetchone()
        new = conn.execute("SELECT decision_id FROM decisions WHERE decision_id=?",
                           (req.new_decision_id,)).fetchone()
        if not old or not new:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Decision not found")
        conn.execute("""UPDATE decisions
            SET superseded_by=?, superseded_at=?, superseded_reason=?
            WHERE decision_id=?""",
            (req.new_decision_id, datetime.now().isoformat(),
             req.reason, req.old_decision_id))
        conn.commit()
    return {"ok": True}
snippets.explanation: Reversing a decision is a link, not a delete. Both decisions are verified to exist, then the old one gets a superseded_by pointer, timestamp, and reason. The superseded decision immediately drops out of get_context (which filters superseded_by IS NULL) but stays fully queryable and explainable — so the history of how thinking changed is never lost.

snippets.title: explain — human-readable writeup with supersede flag
snippets.feature: qi_explain — render any record as markdown
snippets.explanation: qi_explain turns a raw row into a readable briefing for a decision, feature, session or project. For decisions it surfaces the code, scope, rationale and a prominent SUPERSEDED warning if the decision was later reversed — so an agent reading it can never act on stale guidance without seeing that it was overturned. Citations point back to the source id.

snippets.title: Strict-JSON evaluation contract
snippets.feature: Cross-project relevance judging with a local model
snippets.code:
_SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    "You are evaluating whether a software feature from one project is relevant "
    "to another. Output MUST be valid JSON matching this schema exactly:\n"
    '{"relevance_score": float 0.0-1.0, "recommendation": "adopt"|"adapt"|"skip"|"discuss", '
    '"reasoning": "string max 200 chars", "confidence": float 0.0-1.0}\n'
    "Return ONLY the JSON object, no prose, no markdown, no code block.")

def _parse_eval_response(raw):
    cleaned = re.sub(r"```(?:json)?", "", raw).strip().strip("`").strip()
    try:
        data = json.loads(cleaned)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return None
    score, rec = data.get("relevance_score"), data.get("recommendation")
    if not isinstance(score, (int, float)) or rec not in ("adopt","adapt","skip","discuss"):
        return None
    return data
snippets.explanation: When a feature is logged, the engine asks the local eval model whether each other project should adopt/adapt/skip/discuss it. The prompt pins a strict JSON schema and the parser defends against the usual LLM noise — markdown fences, stray backticks — and validates the score type and the recommendation enum. Anything malformed returns None, which triggers exactly one retry before a safe fallback.

snippets.title: History-aware propagation across projects
snippets.feature: Recommendations consistent with how a project decided before
snippets.code:
for target in target_projects:
    with open_brain_db() as conn:
        history_rows = conn.execute("""
            SELECT fe.recommendation, fe.reasoning, f.name as feature_name, f.domain
            FROM feature_evaluations fe
            JOIN features f ON f.feature_id = fe.feature_id
            WHERE fe.target_project = ?
            ORDER BY fe.evaluated_at DESC
            LIMIT ?""", (target["project_id"], MAX_HISTORY)).fetchall()
    history = [dict(r) for r in history_rows]
    eval_dict = await _evaluate_one(feature, source_project, target, eval_model, history)
    results.append(eval_dict)
# ... INSERT all results, then UPDATE features SET propagated = 1
snippets.explanation: For every active project other than the source, the engine pulls that target's last MAX_HISTORY (5) evaluations and feeds them to the model as soft context, so its judgement stays consistent with how the project has actually decided in the past. All evaluations are written to feature_evaluations and the feature is marked propagated, ready for the owner to confirm in the pending-review queue.

snippets.title: Load a provider from the DB by role
snippets.feature: Zero hardcoded model config
snippets.explanation: The Brain never names a model in code. Roles ('embed', 'eval', 'general', 'heavy') resolve to whatever provider row holds that role in the llm_providers table, and provider_type maps to a Python adapter class. Swapping the embedder or the evaluation model is a single UPDATE — and API keys are referenced by env-var NAME (api_key_env), never stored as a value.

snippets.title: Local embeddings via nomic-embed-text
snippets.feature: Free, local 768-dim vectors
snippets.code:
async def embed(self, text: str) -> list[float]:
    payload = {"model": self.model_name, "prompt": text}  # nomic-embed-text
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=self.timeout_s) as client:
        resp = await client.post(f"{self.base_url}/api/embeddings", json=payload)
        resp.raise_for_status()
        return resp.json()["embedding"]
snippets.explanation: Every vector in the four ChromaDB collections is produced here, by nomic-embed-text running locally through Ollama's /api/embeddings endpoint (768-dimensional output). Because it is local, the Brain's entire semantic-memory layer runs at zero marginal cost and with no external dependency or API key.

snippets.title: Strip the thinking, keep the answer
snippets.feature: Clean output from local reasoning models
snippets.explanation: Reasoning models like deepseek-r1 and qwen3 emit a <think>...</think> chain-of-thought before their answer. The provider strips that block out before returning, so the feature engine's strict-JSON parser sees only the final JSON object — not the model's internal monologue.

snippets.title: A tool definition (qi_log_decision)
snippets.feature: 12-tool MCP schema returned on tools/list
snippets.explanation: This is one of the 12 entries in the TOOLS list the MCP server returns on tools/list. The inputSchema tells a Claude session exactly what arguments the tool takes, which are required, and which fields are enums — so the model can call qi_log_decision correctly without reading any Brain source.

snippets.title: match/case router to the FastAPI endpoints
snippets.feature: Thin stdio-to-HTTP forwarding (Supplement A I-01)
snippets.code:
async def dispatch_tool(name: str, args: dict) -> dict:
    match name:
        case "qi_get_context":          return await _post("/api/context", args)
        case "qi_log_decision":         return await _post("/api/log_decision", args)
        case "qi_log_feature":          return await _post("/api/log_feature", args)
        case "qi_search_memory":        return await _post("/api/search_memory", args)
        case "qi_log_session":          return await _post("/api/log_session", args)
        case "qi_get_ecosystem_snapshot": return await _get("/api/ecosystem_snapshot")
        case "qi_supersede_decision":   return await _post("/api/supersede_decision", args)
        case "qi_explain":              return await _post("/api/explain", args)
        case _:                          return {"ok": False, "error": f"Unknown tool: {name}"}
snippets.explanation: The entire MCP server is a router like this: each tool name maps to a single HTTP call against the FastAPI app on :9011. Because no logic lives here, the Brain can be upgraded or restarted without changing the MCP registration, and the same operations are equally available to non-Claude callers over plain REST. A ConnectError surfaces as a clean 'Brain API unreachable at :9011' message.

snippets.title: Windows-safe stdio loop
snippets.feature: JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout without the Proactor crash
snippets.explanation: MCP speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio. On Windows, reading stdin directly with asyncio's Proactor loop crashes; routing the blocking sys.stdin.readline through run_in_executor sidesteps that bug. Notifications (like notifications/initialized) return None and produce no reply, per the MCP spec.

snippets.title: Idempotent bootstrap step decorator
snippets.feature: Safe-to-re-run 10-step initialization
snippets.explanation: Bootstrap is a 10-step pipeline (create DB, seed agents/providers/config/projects, init Chroma, ingest docs + summaries, seed decisions, log completion). Each step is wrapped so a completed step is skipped on re-run and its outcome is recorded in bootstrap_log. This makes setup safe to run repeatedly and makes a half-finished bootstrap resumable rather than destructive.

snippets.title: Document index migration (the knowledge graph)
snippets.feature: Documentation Brain — catalog + typed edges
snippets.code:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS doc_relationships (
    rel_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    src_type   TEXT NOT NULL,   -- doc|project|decision|feature|session
    src_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
    edge_type  TEXT NOT NULL,   -- belongs_to|references|links_to|mentions|supersedes|describes
    dst_type   TEXT NOT NULL,
    dst_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
    weight     REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.0,
    source     TEXT,            -- path|wikilink|mention|manual
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    UNIQUE(src_type, src_id, edge_type, dst_type, dst_id)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rel_src ON doc_relationships(src_type, src_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rel_dst ON doc_relationships(dst_type, dst_id);
snippets.explanation: The Documentation Brain turns the flat docs catalog (921 rows) into a graph. doc_relationships holds typed, weighted edges between docs, projects, decisions, features and sessions — belongs_to, references, mentions, supersedes. The UNIQUE constraint makes edge insertion idempotent, and the two indexes make both 'what does X link to?' and 'what links to X?' fast. 2,203 edges currently connect the ecosystem's documentation.

snippets.title: Poller configuration in the DB
snippets.feature: Background poller — stays current without a push
snippets.code:
INBOX_DIR = Path(r"C:\QIH\engine\brain\inbox")

# Poll sources per project:
#   <project_path>/data/state.json or status.json   — project state file
#   <project_path>/data/tasks.json                  — task board (QI Hive only)
#   git log --since=<last_check>                     — recent commits
#
# Configuration (brain_config table):
#   poll_interval_s      — seconds between cycles (default 300)
#   poll_min_file_age_s  — only process files older than this (default 60)
#   poll_enabled         — '1' to run, '0' to pause (default 1)
snippets.explanation: The poller is what keeps the Brain current between sessions. As a daemon thread it wakes every poll_interval_s (300), and for each registered project reads its state file and recent git commits, plus any JSON dropped in the inbox/ folder that is older than poll_min_file_age_s (the age check avoids reading a half-written file). All settings live in the brain_config table, so polling can be paused or retuned without a restart. 18,718 cycles are logged in poll_log.
